blocks.text: This page tracks the Mission MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $787,800 for a typical home, down 11.9% over twelve months.
Mission benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Mission home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $787,800 in October 2026. That is little changed at −1.2% on the month, down 5.3% over three months, down 4.8% over six months and down 11.9% over the year. Over three years it is down 14.0%, and over five years down 16.2%.
The weakest one-year move in Mission was for a detached home homes at −13.1%; the strongest was a townhouse at −6.1%.
The gap between a detached home ($883,300) and an apartment ($396,200) is $487,100, and a townhouse ($606,100) sits $209,900 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, Mission is 8.4% below. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 11.9% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Mission ranks 6 by all-home benchmark, with Surrey above it at $899,900 and Abbotsford below it at $702,800.

Detached homes in Mission: benchmark $883,300, little changed at −0.7% in a month, down 5.5% in three months, down 5.0% in six months, down 13.1% in a year, down 10.8% in three years and down 13.8% in five. That is 31.7% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in Mission: benchmark $606,100, down 1.9% in a month, down 3.9% in three months, down 5.0% in six months, down 6.1% in a year, down 6.0% in three years and up 2.1% in five. That is 18.3% below the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in Mission: benchmark $396,200, down 3.7% in a month, down 7.0% in three months, down 8.0% in six months, down 8.2% in a year, down 12.0% in three years and up 3.1% in five. That is 14.0% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, Mission had 17 detached sales (29 a year earlier), 5 townhouse sales (10 a year earlier) and 4 apartment sales (4 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 211 detached (about 286 a year earlier), 66 townhouse (about 43 a year earlier) and 56 apartment (about 38 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 8.1% for detached, 7.6% for townhouse and 7.1% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical Mission home is worth about $106,400 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $894,200. By type, detached homes lost about $133,200, from $1,016,500 to $883,300, townhouses lost about $39,400, from $645,500 to $606,100, and apartments lost about $35,400, from $431,600 to $396,200 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $827,500 six months ago and near $916,000 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $39,700 below the six-month mark and about $128,200 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the Mission benchmark is about $72,200 below the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $24,600 below.
Mission sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 327 Mission houses sold at a median of $910,000 (middle half $780,000 to $1.09M), half of them within 35 days. 41 condos sold at a median of $464,700 (middle half $400,000 to $518,000), half within 33 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $970,000 to $835,000 between November–January and August–October (75 and 57 sales).

blocks.text: What the Mission figure is
The $787,800 Mission figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Fraser Valley Real Estate Board for October 2026.
